questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 3
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: The Tamil version of ___________ John Abraham-starrer Madras Cafe __________ cleared by the Censor Board with no cuts last week, but the film's distributors _________ no takers among the exhibitors for a  release in Tamil  Nadu _______ this Friday.

solution.concept: Verbal Aptitude - Articles, Tense, and Prepositions
solution.markdown:
### 1. Slot-by-Slot Grammatical Analysis
The sentence is:
$$\text{\"The Tamil version of } \underline{\hspace{1.5cm}} \text{ John Abraham-starrer Madras Cafe } \underline{\hspace{1.5cm}} \text{ cleared by the Censor Board with no cuts last week, but the film's distributors } \underline{\hspace{1.5cm}} \text{ no takers among the exhibitors for a release in Tamil Nadu } \underline{\hspace{1.5cm}} \text{ this Friday.\"}$$

* **First blank**: Before a specific, already-identified film title ("John Abraham-starrer Madras Cafe"), the definite article **the** is required. (Option C: "the".)
* **Second blank**: The film was cleared in the past; the passive voice with past tense requires **was**. (Option C: "was".)
* **Third blank**: The distributors "found" (discovered/had) no takers; past tense **found**. (Option C: "found".)
* **Fourth blank**: A release scheduled for "this Friday" takes the preposition **on** ("on this Friday"). (Option C: "on".)

### 2. Option Evaluation
* **Option A (Mr., was, found, on)**: "Mr." is not an article and cannot precede a film title.
* **Option B (a, was, found, at)**: "a" is indefinite; the film is specific. "at this Friday" is ungrammatical.
* **Option C (the, was, found, on)**: **Correct** on all four slots.
* **Option D (a, being, find, at)**: Wrong tense and article; "find" does not agree with past context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option C (the, was, found, on)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 4
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: If ROAD is written as URDG, then SWAN should be written as:

solution.markdown:
### 1. Decoding the Cipher Rule
We are given:
$$\text{ROAD} \mapsto \text{URDG}$$

Map each letter to its position in the alphabet (A=1, ..., Z=26):
* R(18) $\to$ U(21): shift $+3$
* O(15) $\to$ R(18): shift $+3$
* A(1) $\to$ D(4): shift $+3$
* D(4) $\to$ G(7): shift $+3$

The cipher is a constant Caesar shift of $+3$.

### 2. Encoding SWAN
Apply the same $+3$ shift:
* S(19) $\to$ V(22)
* W(23) $\to$ Z(26)
* A(1) $\to$ D(4)
* N(14) $\to$ Q(17)

Result:
$$\text{SWAN} \mapsto \text{VZDQ}$$

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A (VXDQ)**: Second letter wrong (X instead of Z).
* **Option B (VZDQ)**: **Correct**; matches the $+3$ shift.
* **Option C (VZDP)**: Last letter wrong (P instead of Q).
* **Option D (UXDQ)**: First/second letters wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (VZDQ)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 5
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: A function f(x) is linear and has a value of 29 at x= -2 and 39 at x=3. Find its value at x=5.

solution.markdown:
### 1. Determining the Linear Function
A linear function has the form:
$$f(x) = mx + c$$

Given:
$$f(-2) = 29, \quad f(3) = 39$$

Slope:
$$m = \frac{f(3) - f(-2)}{3 - (-2)} = \frac{39 - 29}{5} = \frac{10}{5} = 2$$

Using $f(-2) = 29$:
$$29 = 2(-2) + c \implies 29 = -4 + c \implies c = 33$$

So:
$$f(x) = 2x + 33$$

### 2. Evaluating at x = 5
$$f(5) = 2(5) + 33 = 10 + 33 = 43$$

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A (59)**: Incorrect extrapolation.
* **Option B (45)**: Arithmetic slip.
* **Option C (43)**: **Correct**; $2(5)+33 = 43$.
* **Option D (35)**: Underestimates.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option C (43)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 6
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
Alexander turned his attention towards India, since he had conquered Persia.
Which one of the statement below is logically valid and can be inferred from the above sentence?
options: Alexander would not have turned his attention towards India had he not conquered Persia.
Alexander was not ready to rest on his laurels, and wanted to march to India.
Alexander was completely in control of his army and could command it to move towards India.
Since Alexander?s kingdom extended to Indian borders after the conquest of Persia, he was keen to move further.

solution.markdown:
### 1. Premise Analysis
The given sentence is:
$$\text{\"Alexander turned his attention towards India, since he had conquered Persia.\"}$$

The word "since" establishes a causal link: the conquest of Persia is the reason/cause for turning attention towards India. Formally:
$$\text{Conquered Persia} \implies \text{Turned attention to India}$$

### 2. Logical Inference
From $P \implies Q$ (where $P$ = conquered Persia, $Q$ = turned attention to India), the contrapositive is valid:
$$\neg P \implies \neg Q$$

That is: had Alexander NOT conquered Persia, he would NOT have turned his attention towards India. This matches Option A.

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A**: "Alexander would not have turned his attention towards India had he not conquered Persia." — **Correct**; valid contrapositive.
* **Option B**: Introduces "rest on his laurels" and "march" — not stated in the premise.
* **Option C**: "completely in control of his army" — unsupported.
* **Option D**: "kingdom extended to Indian borders" — unsupported geographic claim.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option A**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 7
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
Most experts feel that in spite of possessing all the technical skills required to be a batsman of the highest order he is unlikely to be so due to lack of requisite temperament. He was guilty of throwing away his wicket several times after working hard to lay a strong foundation. His critics pointed out that until he addressed this problem, success at the highest level will continue to elude him.

Which of the statement(s) below is/are logically valid and can be inferred from the above passage?

i. He was already a successful batsman at the highest level.
ii. He has to improve his temperament in order to become a great batsman.
iii. He failed to make many of his good starts count.
iv. Improving his technical skills will guarantee success.

solution.markdown:
### 1. Premise Deconstruction
The passage states:
1. The player has all technical skills to be a top batsman but is unlikely to reach that level due to lack of requisite temperament.
2. He was guilty of throwing away his wicket several times after working hard to lay a strong foundation.
3. Critics: until he addresses this problem, success at the highest level will continue to elude him.

### 2. Statement-by-Statement Evaluation
* **(i) "He was already a successful batsman at the highest level."** — Invalid. The passage says success "will continue to elude him"; he is not yet successful at the highest level.
* **(ii) "He has to improve his temperament in order to become a great batsman."** — Valid. The passage attributes his shortfall to lack of temperament and says addressing the problem is needed for success.
* **(iii) "He failed to make many of his good starts count."** — Valid. "Throwing away his wicket several times after working hard to lay a strong foundation" directly means good starts were wasted.
* **(iv) "Improving his technical skills will guarantee success."** — Invalid. The passage says he already possesses all required technical skills; the deficiency is temperament, not technique.

### 3. Conclusion
Statements (ii) and (iii) are valid.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B ((ii) and (iii))**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 8
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: The exports and imports (in crores of Rs.) of a country from the year 2000 to 2007 are given in the following bar chart. In which year is the combined percentage increase in imports and exports the highest?

solution.concept: Quantitative Aptitude - Bar Chart Percentage Increase
solution.markdown:
### 1. Method
For each year, compute the combined percentage increase in exports and imports relative to the previous year:
$$\text{Combined \% increase} = \frac{(E_{\text{curr}} - E_{\text{prev}}) + (I_{\text{curr}} - I_{\text{prev}})}{E_{\text{prev}} + I_{\text{prev}}} \times 100$$

Equivalently, compute the total (exports + imports) for consecutive years and find the year with the largest relative jump in the combined total.

### 2. Application to the Chart
Reading the bar values for exports and imports (in crores of Rs.) from 2000–2007 and computing the year-over-year combined growth:
* 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007 are compared in turn.
* The largest combined percentage increase occurs in **2006**, where both exports and imports rise sharply together relative to 2005.

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A (2007)**: Growth is present but smaller than 2006.
* **Option B (2006)**: **Correct**; highest combined percentage increase.
* **Option C (2005)**: Moderate growth.
* **Option D (2004)**: Lower growth.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (2006)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 9
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: Choose the most appropriate equation for the function drawn as a thick line, in the plot below.

solution.concept: Quantitative Aptitude - Absolute Value Function & Graph
solution.markdown:
### 1. Piecewise Analysis of x = -(y - |y|)
Consider the equation:
$$x = -(y - |y|) = |y| - y$$

* **Case y $\geq$ 0**: $|y| = y$, so
  $$x = y - y = 0$$
  This is the non-negative $y$-axis (vertical ray upward from origin).

* **Case y < 0**: $|y| = -y$, so
  $$x = -y - y = -2y = 2|y| > 0$$
  This is a ray in the fourth quadrant (positive $x$, negative $y$), making a $45^\circ$-type line $x = -2y$.

Thus the graph consists of the positive $y$-axis for $y \geq 0$ and a ray going down-right for $y < 0$, matching the thick line described.

### 2. Option Evaluation
* **Option A ($x = y - |y|$)**: Gives $x = 0$ for $y \geq 0$ and $x = 2y$ (negative) for $y < 0$ — opposite horizontal direction.
* **Option B ($x = -(y - |y|)$)**: **Correct**; matches the derived piecewise graph.
* **Option C ($x = y + |y|$)**: Gives $x = 2y$ for $y \geq 0$ and $x = 0$ for $y < 0$ — different orientation.
* **Option D ($x = -(y + |y|)$)**: Gives $x = -2y$ for $y \geq 0$ and $x = 0$ for $y < 0$ — different orientation.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B ($x = -(y - |y|)$)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 10
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
The head of a newly formed government desires to appoint five of the six selected members P, Q, R, S, T,and U to portfolios of Home, Power, Defense, Telecom, and Finance. U does not want any portfolio if S gets one of the five. R wants either Home or Finance or no portfolio. Q says that if S gets either Power or Telecom, then she must get the other one. T insists on a portfolio if P gets one.
Which is the valid distribution of portfolios?
options: P- Home, Q - Power, R - Defense, S - Telecom, T - Finance
R- Home, S - Power, P - Defense, Q - Telecom, T - Finance
P- Home, Q - Power, T - Defense, S - Telecom, U - Finance
Q- Home, U - Power, T - Defense, R - Telecom, P - Finance

solution.markdown:
### 1. Constraints Restated
Five portfolios: Home, Power, Defense, Telecom, Finance assigned to five of six members P, Q, R, S, T, U.
* U does not want any portfolio if S gets one.
* R wants either Home, Finance, or no portfolio.
* Q: if S gets Power or Telecom, Q must get the other.
* T insists on a portfolio if P gets one.

### 2. Testing Each Option
* **Option A**: P-Home, Q-Power, R-Defense, S-Telecom, T-Finance. R gets Defense — violates R's constraint (only Home/Finance/none).
* **Option B**: R-Home, S-Power, P-Defense, Q-Telecom, T-Finance. R gets Home (ok). S gets Power so Q must get Telecom (ok). P gets Defense so T must get a portfolio (T-Finance, ok). U not assigned and S got one (ok). **Valid.**
* **Option C**: P-Home, Q-Power, T-Defense, S-Telecom, U-Finance. Q gets Power and S gets Telecom; Q's rule says if S gets Telecom, Q must get Power — ok, but U gets Finance while S got a portfolio — violates U's constraint.
* **Option D**: Q-Home, U-Power, T-Defense, R-Telecom, P-Finance. R gets Telecom — violates R's constraint.

### 3. Conclusion
Only Option B satisfies every constraint.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 1
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence.
The official answered __________ that the complaints of the citizen would be looked into.

solution.concept: Verbal Aptitude - Adverb Selection (Respectfully vs. Respectably)
solution.markdown:
### 1. Semantic Distinction
* **respectably**: in a manner worthy of respect; decently (describes manner of dress/behavior quality).
* **respectfully**: with respect; showing deference/politeness.
* **reputably**: with a good reputation.
* **respectively**: in the order given.

### 2. Context
"The official answered ________ that the complaints of the citizen would be looked into." The official is showing deference/politeness in addressing citizens' complaints, so **respectfully** is appropriate.

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A (respectably)**: Wrong nuance (decency, not deference).
* **Option B (respectfully)**: **Correct**.
* **Option C (reputably)**: Unrelated to manner of answering.
* **Option D (respectively)**: Used for ordered correspondence, not here.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (respectfully)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 2
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: Choose the statement where underlined word is used correctly.
options: The minister $\underline{\text{insured}}$ the victims that everything would be all right.
He $\underline{\text{ensured}}$ that the company will not have to bear any loss.
The actor got himself $\underline{\text{ensured}}$ against any accident.
The teacher $\underline{\text{insured}}$ students of good results.

solution.markdown:
### 1. Meaning Distinction
* **ensure**: to make certain/sure that something happens.
* **insure**: to provide insurance coverage against loss.

### 2. Sentence-by-Sentence Evaluation
* Option A: "The minister insured the victims that everything would be all right." — Wrong; should be "assured/ensured," not "insured."
* **Option B**: "He ensured that the company will not have to bear any loss." — **Correct**; "ensured" = made sure.
* Option C: "The actor got himself ensured against any accident." — Wrong; should be "insured."
* Option D: "The teacher insured students of good results." — Wrong; should be "assured."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 3
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: which word is not a synonym for the word vernacular?

solution.markdown:
### 1. Definition
**Vernacular** = native, indigenous, regional, colloquial (the everyday language of a place/people).

### 2. Option Evaluation

* **indigenous** (Option B): Synonym.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 4
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: Mr. Vivek walks 6 meters North-east, then turns and walks 6 meters South-east, both at 60 degrees to east. He further moves 2 meters South and 4 meters West. What is the straight distance in meters between the point he started from and the point he finally reached?

solution.markdown:
### 1. Component-wise Walk
Angles are measured from East; NE/SE at $60^\circ$ to East.

* **Leg 1**: 6 m NE at $60^\circ$: $(6\cos60^\circ,\, 6\sin60^\circ) = (3,\, 3\sqrt{3})$.
* **Leg 2**: 6 m SE at $60^\circ$: $(6\cos60^\circ,\, -6\sin60^\circ) = (3,\, -3\sqrt{3})$.
* **Leg 3**: 2 m South: $(0,\, -2)$.
* **Leg 4**: 4 m West: $(-4,\, 0)$.

Total displacement:
$$\Delta x = 3 + 3 + 0 - 4 = 2$$
$$\Delta y = 3\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3} - 2 + 0 = -2$$

### 2. Straight-line Distance
$$d = \sqrt{(\Delta x)^2 + (\Delta y)^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}$$

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A ($2\sqrt{2}$)**: **Correct**.
* **Option B ($2$)**: Only one component.
* **Option C ($\sqrt{2}$)**: Half of correct.
* **Option D ($1/\sqrt{2}$)**: Inverted.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option A ($2\sqrt{2}$)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 5
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: Four cards are randomly selected from a pack of 52 cards. If the first two cards are kings, what is the probability that the third card is a king?

solution.markdown:
### 1. Setup
A standard 52-card deck has 4 kings. The first two drawn cards are kings (given). Remaining deck: 50 cards with 2 kings.

### 2. Conditional Probability
$$P(\text{3rd is king} \mid \text{first two are kings}) = \frac{\text{remaining kings}}{\text{remaining cards}} = \frac{2}{50}$$

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A ($4/52$)**: Ignores conditioning.
* **Option B ($2/50$)**: **Correct**.
* **Option C ($(1/52)^2$)**: Wrong model.
* **Option D ($(1/52)(1/51)(1/50)$)**: Wrong model.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B ($2/50$)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 6

**Dreary** = dull, bleak, depressing, dismal.

### 2. Option Evaluation

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 7
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
The given question is followed by two statements; select the most appropriate option that solves the question.
Capacity of a solution tank A is 70% of the capacity of tank B. How many gallons of solution are in tank A and tank B?
Statements:

I. Tank A is 80% full and tank B is 40% full.
II. Tank A if full contains 14,000 gallons of solution.
options: Either statement I or II alone is sufficient.
Both the statements I and II together are sufficient.

solution.markdown:
### 1. Problem
Capacity of tank A = 70% of capacity of tank B. Find gallons in A and B.
* Statement I: A is 80% full, B is 40% full.
* Statement II: A full contains 14,000 gallons.

### 2. Sufficiency Analysis
* Statement I alone: Gives fill percentages but not absolute capacities. Insufficient.
* Statement II alone: Gives capacity of A = 14,000 gal, so B = 14,000/0.7. But fill levels unknown, so current amounts unknown. Insufficient.
* Both together: A capacity = 14,000; B capacity = 14,000/0.7 = 20,000. A content = 0.8×14,000 = 11,200; B content = 0.4×20,000 = 8,000. Sufficient.

### 3. Conclusion
Both statements together are sufficient.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option D (Both the statements I and II together are sufficient)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 8
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: How many four digit numbers can be formed with the 10 digits 0,1,2, . . . ,9 if no number can start with 0 and if repetitions are not allowed?

solution.markdown:
### 1. Counting
Four-digit number, no leading zero, no repetition among 10 digits.
* Thousands place: 9 choices (1–9).
* Hundreds: 9 choices (0–9 except chosen) — since 0 now allowed.
* Tens: 8 choices.
* Units: 7 choices.

Total:
$$N = 9 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 = 4536$$

### 2. Option Evaluation
* **Option A (14523)**: Too large.
* **Option B (4536)**: **Correct**.
* **Option C (4578)**: Arithmetic error.
* **Option D (9853)**: Not matching.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (4536)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 9
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following table giving sales data of five types of batteries for years 2006 to 2012:

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|} \hline \text{Year} & \text{Type I} & \text{Type II} & \text{Type III} & \text{Type IV} & \text{Type V} \\ \hline 2006 & 75 & 144 & 144 & 102 & 108 \\ \hline 2007 & 90 & 126 & 102 & 84 & 126 \\ \hline 2008 & 96 & 114 & 75 & 105 & 135 \\ \hline 2009 & 105 & 60 & 165 & 45 & 120 \\ \hline 2010 & 90 & 75 & 135 & 75 & 90 \\ \hline 2011 & 105 & 60 & 165 & 45 & 120 \\ \hline 2012 & 115 & 85 & 160 & 100 & 145 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Out of the following, which type of battery achieved highest growth between the years 2006 and 2012?

solution.concept: Quantitative Aptitude - Percentage Growth from Tabular Data
solution.markdown:
### 1. Growth Calculation (2006 → 2012)
$$\text{Growth} = \frac{\text{Sales}_{2012} - \text{Sales}_{2006}}{\text{Sales}_{2006}} \times 100$$

* Type I: $(115-75)/75 = 40/75 = 53.3\%$
* Type II: $(85-144)/144 = -41.0\%$
* Type III: $(160-144)/144 = 11.1\%$
* Type IV: $(100-102)/102 = -2.0\%$
* Type V: $(145-108)/108 = 34.3\%$

### 2. Conclusion
Highest growth is Type I at $53.3\%$.

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A (Type V)**: 34.3% — lower.
* **Option B (Type III)**: 11.1% — lower.
* **Option C (Type II)**: Negative growth.
* **Option D (Type I)**: **Correct**; 53.3%.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option D (Type I)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 2 | GA | Question: 10
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: There are 16 teachers who can teach Thermodynamics (TD), 11 who can teach Electrical Sciences (ES), and 5 who can teach both TD and Engineering  Mechanics (EM). There are a total of 40 teachers, 6 cannot teach any of the three subjects, i.e. EM, ES or TD. 6 can teach only ES. 4 can teach all three subjects, i.e. EM, ES, and TD. 4 can teach ES and TD. How many can teach both ES and EM but not TD?

solution.concept: Quantitative Aptitude - Set Theory / Venn Diagram (Three Subjects)
solution.markdown:
### 1. Region Setup
Let regions for TD, ES, EM (8 regions). Given:
* Total teachers = 40; none = 6 ⇒ union = 34.
* $|TD| = 16$, $|ES| = 11$.
* Only ES = 6.
* All three = 4.
* ES ∩ TD = 4 (so ES∩TD only = 0).
* TD ∩ EM = 5 (so TD∩EM only = 1).

### 2. Solving for ES ∩ EM (not TD)
From $|ES| = 11$:
$$\text{only ES} + \text{ES\&TD only} + \text{ES\&EM only} + \text{all three} = 11$$
$$6 + 0 + y + 4 = 11 \implies y = 1$$

Thus teachers who can teach both ES and EM but not TD = 1.

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A (1)**: **Correct**.
* **Option B (2)**: Overcount.
* **Option C (3)**: Overcount.
* **Option D (4)**: Equals triple intersection.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option A (1)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 1
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
A student is required to demonstrate a high level of comprehension of the subject, especially in the social sciences.

**Comprehension** = understanding; the ability to grasp meaning.

### 2. Option Evaluation
* **understanding** (A): **Correct** closest synonym.
* **meaning** (B): Related but not the closest (comprehension is the act, meaning is the content).
* **concentration** (C): Unrelated.

questions.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 2
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence.
One of his biggest ______ was his ability to forgive.

solution.markdown:
### 1. Context
"One of his biggest ______ was his ability to forgive." Forgiving is a positive trait, so the blank needs a positive noun.

### 2. Option Evaluation
* **vice** (A): Negative trait — opposite.
* **virtues** (B): **Correct**; positive moral quality.
* **choices** (C): Grammatically awkward ("one of his biggest choices was his ability").
* **strength** (D): Plausible but "virtues" is the established collocation.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (virtues)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 3
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
Rajan was not happy that Sajan decided to do the project on his own. On observing his unhappiness, Sajan explained to Rajan that he preferred to work independently.
Which one of the statements below is logically valid and can be inferred from the above sentences?
options: Rajan has decided to work only in a group.
Rajan and Sajan were formed into a group against their wishes.
Sajan had decided to give in to Rajan?s request to work with him.
Rajan had believed that Sajan and he would be working together.

solution.markdown:
### 1. Premise
Rajan was unhappy that Sajan decided to do the project on his own. On observing this, Sajan explained he preferred to work independently.

### 2. Inference
Rajan's unhappiness implies he had expected/assumed they would work together. Sajan's preference for independence contradicts that expectation. Thus Rajan had believed Sajan and he would be working together.

### 3. Option Evaluation
* **Option A**: "Rajan has decided to work only in a group." — Not inferable.
* **Option B**: "Rajan and Sajan were formed into a group against their wishes." — Not stated.
* **Option C**: "Sajan had decided to give in to Rajan's request." — Contradicts (Sajan preferred independence).
* **Option D**: "Rajan had believed that Sajan and he would be working together." — **Correct**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option D**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 4
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: If $y=5x^2+3$, then the tangent at $x=0,y=3$

solution.markdown:
### 1. Differentiation
$$y = 5x^2 + 3$$
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 10x$$

At $x = 0$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx}\bigg|_{x=0} = 10(0) = 0$$

A slope of 0 means the tangent is horizontal, i.e., parallel to the $x$-axis. At $x=0$, $y=3$, point $(0,3)$.

### 2. Option Evaluation
* **Option A**: passes through (0,0) — False (tangent is y=3).
* **Option B**: slope +1 — False (slope 0).
* **Option C**: parallel to x-axis — **Correct**.
* **Option D**: slope -1 — False.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option C (is parallel to the x-axis)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 5
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: A foundry has a fixed daily cost of Rs 50,000 whenever it operates and a variable cost of Rs 800Q, where Q is the daily production in tonnes. What is the cost of production in Rs per tonne for a daily production of 100 tonnes?

solution.concept: Quantitative Aptitude - Unit Cost (Fixed + Variable Cost)
solution.markdown:
### 1. Cost Computation
Daily cost:
$$C(Q) = 50000 + 800Q$$
For $Q = 100$ tonnes:
$$C(100) = 50000 + 800(100) = 50000 + 80000 = 130000 \text{ Rs}$$

Cost per tonne:
$$\frac{130000}{100} = 1300 \text{ Rs/tonne}$$

### 2. Conclusion
The cost of production is 1300 Rs per tonne.

Therefore, the correct answer is **1300**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 6
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml: Find the odd one in the following group: ALRVX, EPVZB, ITZDF, OYEIK

solution.concept: Quantitative Aptitude - Pattern Recognition (Odd One Out)
solution.markdown:
### 1. Pattern Analysis
Check letter-position increments within each group:
* ALRVX: A(1)→L(12): +11, L→R: +6, R→V: +4, V→X: +2.
* EPVZB: E(5)→P(16): +11, P→V: +6, V→Z: +4, Z→B: +2 (wrap).
* ITZDF: I(9)→T(20): +11, T→Z: +6, Z→D: +4 (wrap), D→F: +2.
* OYEIK: O(15)→Y(25): +10 (not +11).

The first three groups follow the increment pattern +11, +6, +4, +2. OYEIK breaks it at the first step (+10 instead of +11).

### 2. Conclusion
The odd one is OYEIK.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option D (OYEIK)**.

questions.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 7
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionHtml:
Anuj, Bhola, Chandan, Dilip, Eswar and Faisal live on different floors in a six-storeyed building (the ground floor is numbered 1, the floor above it 2,and so on). Anuj lives on an even-numbered floor.Bhola does not live on an odd numbered floor. Chandan does not live on any of the floors below Faisal?s floor. Dilip does not live on floor number 2. Eswar does not live on a floor immediately above or immediately below Bhola. Faisal lives three floors above Dilip. Which of the following floor-person combinations is correct?

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Anuj} & \text{Bhola} & \text{Chandan} & \text{Dilip} & \text{Eswar} & \text{Faisal} \\ \hline (A) & 6 & 2 & 5 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline (B) & 2 & 6 & 5 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline (C) & 4 & 2 & 6 & 3 & 1 & 5 \\ \hline (D) & 2 & 4 & 6 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

solution.markdown:
### 1. Constraints
Six people on floors 1–6.
* Anuj: even floor.
* Bhola: not odd.
* Chandan: not below Faisal.
* Dilip: not floor 2.
* Eswar: not immediately above/below Bhola.
* Faisal: 3 floors above Dilip.

### 2. Testing Option B
Option B: Anuj=2, Bhola=6, Chandan=5, Dilip=1, Eswar=3, Faisal=4.
* Anuj even (2) ✓
* Bhola not odd (6) ✓
* Chandan (5) not below Faisal (4) ✓
* Dilip not 2 (1) ✓
* Eswar (3) not adjacent to Bhola (6) ✓
* Faisal (4) = Dilip (1)+3 ✓

All constraints satisfied.

### 3. Conclusion
Option B is the valid distribution.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B**.
